changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `widgets.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8218-studio-property-panel-de-developerize.md`

- names `widgets.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `SchemaForm` + `widgets.tsx` were written for an administrator editing metadata. Studio's interface panel renders the very same form for someone who has never seen a JSON Schema, so four developer habits landed inside an otherwise fully Chinese surface. Same cause, one pass:

### `.changeset/formfieldspec-dependson-5040.md`

- names `widgets.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `FormFieldSpec` — the authoring type for a metadata-admin form layout, the element type of `FormSectionSpec.fields[]` — did not declare `dependsOn`. `widgets.tsx` held a second, inline description of the same object as `WidgetProps.fieldSpec`, and that one did, because two registered widgets read it as their primary configuration: `field-selector` resolves `dependsOn || reference || 'objectName'` to decide whose field catalog to offer, and `dynamic-config` uses it to pick a sub-schema out of `WidgetContext.dynamicSchemas`. One value travelling down one channel, described twice, disagreeing on the one key that decides what those widgets show — so

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `4598f6d29` (merge-base with origin/main): 15 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1140 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1667 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35310651885)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6950d51410a03be669e43757941fbfa82aa34e59`

### ① Derived judgments

1. Clause-② `yes` is RIGHT, re-derived rather than accepted. At the head tree: `packages/app-shell/package.json` is not private, `files` ships `dist`, `exports['.'].types` is `./dist/index.d.ts`, and `build` is a bare `tsc` with `declaration: true` (packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json), so the emitted declarations are TypeScript's own. `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts:379` exports `SchemaForm`; `WidgetContext` is named 0 times in every `packages/*/src/index.ts(x)` barrel (control: 84 `^export` lines in that entry). `SchemaForm.tsx:652` is `export interface SchemaFormProps` carrying `widgetContext?: WidgetContext` at :694, consumed by `export function SchemaForm(props: SchemaFormProps)` at :967 (8 such positions total). I reproduced the mechanism with the real `tsc` (v22 toolchain, scratch model of exactly this shape: interface in widgets.ts, referenced only from an exported SchemaForm signature, barrel exports only SchemaForm): `dist/index.d.ts` names WidgetContext 0 times, `dist/SchemaForm.d.ts` carries `import { type WidgetContext } from './widgets.js'`, and a consumer resolving through the PACKAGE NAME via `exports['.'].types` gets `error TS2741: Property 'conditionScope' is missing ... but required in type 'WidgetContext'` (exit 2) when the member is omitted and exit 0 when supplied. A type reaching an exported signature is emitted into declaration output without any barrel re-export; that is what happens here. Construction-site census verified: exactly two non-test `React.useMemo` sites typed `WidgetContext` (ResourceEditPage.tsx:968, inspectors/ViewVariantInspector.tsx:308); the only non-test `widgetContext=` props are those two hosts plus SchemaForm's internal forwarding, so "compile-enforced at both non-test construction sites" holds.

2. Semver. The changeset declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': minor` and opens with "Breaking for consumers constructing `WidgetContext`", names the REQUIRED member and its literal union, names the transitive route (SchemaForm's widgetContext prop), and states why `minor` (fixed group tracks the objectstack major; `major` forbidden). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` exists at head and says in its own docblock that objectui's breaking changes ship as `minor` with the break spelled out in the body. The changeset's "nothing changes for a consumer that passes no widgetContext" is true: the prop is optional at SchemaForm.tsx:694. Honest at the required level.

3. Table vs the ruling (comment 5716922008), row by row, against `conditionScope.ts` at head: action → `record` (present); validation rule → `record` (keyed `validation: 'record'`; the `__object_validation` anchor row is `none`, and it is never an edit route); hook → `record` (present); flow node → `flattened` (`flow`); permission / RLS → `flattened` (`permission` and `sharing_rule`); page block → `none` (`page: 'none'`) NOW, with the code comment recording objectstack#18554 as the future change and stating the card does not wait on it, and the PR carrying `Fixes #8167` with no dependency; any type without a row → `none` as an explicit row for every registered type plus a runtime `?? 'none'` fallback. No row disagrees with the ruling. Registry reconciliation done statically from register-builtins' import chain: anchors.ts registers 12 types (__object_field, __object_index, __object_validation, action, dashboard, flow, hook, object, page, permission, report, view), default-schemas.ts registers 12 (app, book, dashboard, email_template, page, permission, position, report, skill, tool, translation, view), datasource/register.ts registers 1; the union is 20 unique types, and the table's 31 keys minus the test's 11 RULED_BEYOND_THE_REGISTRY names is exactly those 20. Both exhaustiveness pins hold on the head tree.

4. The absent-context case. `ConditionWidget` reads `context?.conditionScope`; undefined leaves the builder rendered with `scope={undefined}`, so `celAuthoring`'s `hint.scope ?? 'flattened'` answers as before. This is the conservative reading: the ten-odd in-tree SchemaForm mounts that pass no widgetContext (EmbeddedItemEditor, PackageFormDialog, ObjectHooksPanel's fallback, the Action/Hook/Page/Dashboard/Report/ViewColumn inspectors' generic forms) are byte-identical. It is consistent with the ruling's intent because the option-B analysis the ruling adopted (comment 5701370574) named this exact cost in words ("leaves every SchemaForm mount that passes no widgetContext at all still silently flattened") and the ruling said "required at construction", nothing about non-constructing hosts. Treating absence as `none` would have swapped the editor under hosts nobody ruled on. The row-tier curated inspectors hide their own condition keys from their no-context generic forms (ActionDefaultInspector CURATED_FIELDS includes visible and disabled; HookDefaultInspector CURATED_FIELDS includes condition), so no ruled row-tier key is left linting flattened on those hosts. The arm is pinned by the "no WidgetContext at all is byte-for-byte unchanged" case. Correct call.

5. The two changed pins. WidgetContext.catalogUnion.test.tsx PIN E (`{}` became `{ conditionScope: 'flattened' }`): the old assertion "an EMPTY context compiles" is exactly the compile-time break the ruling ordered, so the change is forced by the type; the pin's stated subject (a CATALOG may be absent: `unwiredContext.objectViews ?? NOT_ASKED`) survives verbatim. Legitimate, not a regression cover. SchemaForm.widgetLabelling.test.tsx `Case.ctx` (now Omit of conditionScope from WidgetContext, with `renderCase` supplying `'flattened'` only when a ctx object exists and `undefined` otherwise): the `condition` case has no ctx at head (line 148) and had none at base f0b4979 (line 137), so it still receives NO context and still renders the builder; the cases with `ctx: {}` are non-condition widgets. Legitimate re-home; the pre-existing witness for the no-context arm is intact.

6. Pins witness. Leg C re-derived by reading: the "carries the ruled verdict" case asserts `conditionScopeForMetadataType('action')` is `'record'`; flipping that row to `'flattened'` reds exactly that case and no other (the two exhaustiveness cases read key sets, the unknown-type case reads the fallback). The table's CONTENT is pinned. Both directions are read against `listMetadataResources()` after `import './register-builtins'`: served minus ruled must be empty (a new type reds) and ruled minus served must equal the named RULED_BEYOND_THE_REGISTRY list exactly (a stale row reds). Legs A and B re-derived by reading: removing `scope={conditionScope}` leaves the builder scopeless so the record-reject case fails on the defect itself; making the `none` branch unreachable fails the three none cases. Vitest was not executed here (this checkout has no node_modules); the re-derivation is by reading, stated as such.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@object-ui/app-shell`, with the break ("Breaking for consumers constructing `WidgetContext`", required member `conditionScope: 'record' | 'flattened' | 'none'`, reached through SchemaForm's widgetContext prop) spelled out in the changeset body. Correct for this repo: `major` is forbidden by `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` because the 39-package fixed group tracks the objectstack major, and that gate's own text prescribes exactly this spelling. Consumers passing no widgetContext are unaffected (prop optional); consumers constructing one stop compiling until they state a verdict, as the changeset says.

### ③ Boundary flags

- F1 (most significant, successor card): the ruled `validation → record` row has no live generic-form host through this PR's mechanism. The standalone `validation` kind is retired (ADR-0088; pinned by anchors.validation-retired.test.ts, which also records that `validation` is not in the spec's kind registry), so ResourceEditPage never legitimately receives `type === 'validation'`. The `editAs: 'validation'` anchor opens EmbeddedItemEditor (MetadataDetailDrawer.tsx:123), whose SchemaForm passes no widgetContext (EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx:229) and, with no `validation` entry in FALLBACK_SCHEMAS (only `index`) and none in the server type entries, falls to the raw-JSON editor. Net: the `record` verdict for validation-rule conditions is delivered today only by the curated ObjectValidationsPanel (PR #9494), not by this change; the row is correct as ruled but currently decorative, and the comments in conditionScope.ts ("the standalone edit route an object's embedded validations open under") and in the test's RULED_BEYOND_THE_REGISTRY note misdescribe the mechanism, since the editor that edits them AS `validation` builds no WidgetContext. The ruling's letter (two construction sites) is met; the successor is EmbeddedItemEditor constructing a WidgetContext derived from `editAs`.
- F2: the derivation edge `ResourceEditPage.tsx:975` (`conditionScope: conditionScopeForMetadataType(type)`) is unwitnessed. The new test drives SchemaForm with a hand-built context; no test mounts ResourceEditPage and observes the lint. Leg C proves the table's content is pinned, not that production reads it: a hard-coded `'flattened'` at that line would compile and leave every affected test green. A pin or ablation leg on that edge is owed by a successor.
- F3: type-keyed derivation hands a parent's verdict to nested tiers. The `object` generic form (design mode off) hides only `fields` and `fieldGroups` (CANVAS_OWNED_KEYS), so a nested `validations[].condition` rendered through the repeater inherits `object → none` (plain input, no claim) where the tier verdict is `record`. Before this change it was builder plus flattened (the false green), so this is strictly less wrong, and it is inherent in the ruling's "type being edited" keying rather than a dev error. Recorded so the next reader does not take `none` there as a decision about validation rules.
- F4: the Clause-② probe was re-derived on a `tsc` model of the head-tree shape plus the head-tree source facts, not on a real app-shell dist build (no node_modules in this checkout; building would write into the shared checkout). The dev's real-dist probe is consistent with the model; it was not reproduced byte-for-byte.
- F5: `permission` has a custom EditPage (PermissionMatrixEditPage, services/builtinComponents.tsx), so the `permission: 'flattened'` row is reached only in createMode. Harmless and as ruled; recorded so the row is not read as the RLS editor's live scope (that surface is PermissionAdvancedFacets' own CelPredicateField mounts).
- F6: no tests were executed in this review (no node_modules); all pin and ablation claims were re-derived by reading the head tree.
- F7: the PR reads `mergeable_state: behind` (base moved from f0b4979 to 57c07f0); not a contract matter.
